what: Every call on ATOM's serving path that can stop a thread, and what a simulated run has to do about it. Rows under 'sites' are produced by the scanner in sync_scan.py and classified by hand; rows under 'anchors' are points that are not a call -- a loop gate, a stamp, a compiled-in bound -- and are pinned to a line of text instead.

categories.A: simulated time decides this, not the real clock: a duration that is predicted rather than elapsed, or a reading the result reports
categories.B: parks until another process sends something, with no bound; the call stays as it is and the process says when it is idle
categories.C1: a bound that exists to declare something broken; raise it or switch it off
categories.C2: a bound that sets a cadence; keep the cadence on simulated time and poll briefly for real so the thread stays responsive
categories.ignore: invisible to the simulated result: inside one process, at startup, at shutdown, below the replaced forward pass, or in a backend the simulator substitutes
categories.undecided: the reading depends on a decision that has not been made

boundary: A bounded wait for another process is C1 or C2 by what the bound is for; the same wait without a bound is B. A wait whose peer is a thread of the same process is ignored, because the process is not idle while one of its own threads is parked.
